extras.limits_verbatim: Not S3 — no bucket API, no presigned URLs, so CDN/CF fronting has to go through WebDAV or an rclone `serve` layer. Inode ceilings matter for a 20 TiB corpus of small files: 1,000 K inodes at 10 TB is 1 M files, which a dataset archive of many small parquet/JSON shards will exhaust long before 10 TB. Per-file size not published on the pricing page.

extras.price_verbatim: $5.95/TB/mo at 10 TB ($59.48/mo) and identically at 50 TB ($297.48/mo) — flat rate, unmetered traffic, no volume discount at either end. Tier ladder is 25 GB / 100 GB / 500 GB / 1 TB / 10 TB / 50 TB, so there is NO 5 TB SKU: 5 TB means buying 5× the 1 TB plan ($64.15/mo = $12.83/TB/mo, poor) or 1× the 10 TB plan and using half of it ($5.95/TB/mo paid, $11.90/TB/mo effectively). 20 TB = 2× the 10 TB plan at $119/mo (derived; confirm they allow a second unit). At 1 TB the rate is $12.83/TB/mo, so buying the 10 TB tier is 2.16× cheaper per terabyte than buying the 1 TB tier.
extras.agent_focus: Wave 7 cheap-PAID lane, regional angle: storage sold in RUB / CNY / BRL / INR / ZAR / TRY / PLN / UAH that never appears on Western price lists. Every paid candidate carries price_per_tb_month at USD-converted list price. FX fixed 2026-10-21 from open.er-api.com: RUB 82.5719/USD, CNY 6.6913, BRL 5.0231, INR 94.9952, ZAR 16.3972, TRY 49.5978, PLN 3.8923, UAH 45.0922, EUR 0.89075/USD. Excluded per brief: AWS, Azure, GCP, Alibaba Cloud, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, IDrive e2. Headline result: the true regional floor with genuinely free egress is ~$2.00/TB/mo (Yandex 360 Profi 3 TB on a Russian card) rising to ~$4.17/TB/mo for the same product bought with a foreign card, and ~$5.95-7.56/TB/mo for flat-rate Western-facing file storage (TheHost, Rollin Host). Everything advertised below ~$2/TB/mo in this set is either capacity-capped, egress-metered, or unverifiable marketing.
